title: Mud Where Ice Should Be

flats.narration: Brackish water curls around ridges of mud. A small figure skips along a shell-bank, then stops before your boots sink. "Shells, not that patch," says the guide. "Welcome to the Saltrot." The guide is a Skupper, with bright eyes and strong front fins.

variants.text: Old Ossley steadies his flat boat at the bank while your whole party steps ashore.
Behind you the fold still hums with cold glacier air.
Behind you the linked fold carries the cloud whales' distant song. Its echo still answers from the island.

lesson.narration: A kitsune named Seren Wisp is comparing notes with a young manticore named Pip Thistledown. They wear the Riftseekers' clasps. "I am finding what has moved," says Pip. Seren asks you to hum the hall note, then listen for an answering sound. "A starweaver can learn to answer a rift's hum. That is called Attune. No one here chooses a rift's rules."

variants.text: A kitsune named Seren Wisp and a manticore named Pip Thistledown are checking another displaced route. Seren asks you to compare the sounds with what she taught you before. Pip adds the new place to his notes.

local.narration: The Skupper points to a pale stripe in the mud. "New silt. Covered the path overnight." A traveler has left a bag on a shell-bank that is slowly flooding. Will you help move the bag or mark a safer path?

choices.label: Pass the bag along the shell-bank
Mark the firm shells for the traveler

bag.narration: You pass the bag from hand to hand, keeping your feet on the shells. The guide skips ahead to show the last safe step. The traveler gets their bag back dry.

path.narration: You follow the guide's front fins and lay empty shells along the firm route. The traveler moves the bag without stepping into the soft silt. "Trust a path once," says the Skupper. "Then look again."

flats_rest.narration: You rest above the tide line. Farther along the flats, new silt is hiding old routes. Your guide is ready to show you where to look next. Out past the shell-banks, a tall wooden house stands on stilts. Loose pages keep fluttering out of its top.

choices.label: Climb the ladder to the stilt house

variants.text: The open fold still hums nearby. Its echo offers a return to the glacier.

flats_onward.narration: You step back onto the shells. The Skupper skips ahead and waits at every safe step, front fins tapping, until you catch up.

academy.narration: At the top of the ladder is a classroom with no roof at all, only sky. This school is called the Academy. Here students learn to be a Starweaver, a hero who reads the stars. A dragonling named Professor Nettle stands beside a huge brass telescope. Homework floats up off the desks and drifts away over the flats. Nobody chases it. "It comes down somewhere," says the professor. On a cushion sits a star circlet. Their light lives in that circlet, and a dusk hood worn beside it starts to itch. "Anyone who wants the circlet," says Professor Nettle, "may try it on."

variants.text: Professor Nettle waves from beside the big brass telescope. "Back at the Academy! Mind the homework." A page floats past your nose and off over the flats. The star circlet waits on its cushion for anyone who wants to try it on.

academy_stars.narration: Professor Nettle lets you look through the telescope. Even by day, the stars are so close you could count their points. Then the telescope sneezes. Brass rattles. Dust puffs out of the far end. "Bless you," says the professor, to the telescope. "It does that when it sees something new."

llmHints.tone: Warm, funny, curious, with real consequences. Describe actions and sensory details directly. Short dialogue. Never use "the kind of thing that", "the sort of thing that", or "it was X, the type of thing that makes you Y" comparisons. Let a character act instead of explaining how the reader should feel.
llmHints.vocabulary: Read aloud to an eight-year-old. Concrete words, short sentences, distinct voices.
